trap_mechanism: Every distractor is a true statement about the topic; only one answers the question actually asked, so recognition feels like knowing.
how_to_spot: Prose options, no lists, no negation word.
step_1: Name the single thing the stem asks for
step_2: Reject options that are true but answer a different question
step_3: Match the survivor to the NCERT line that states it
step_4: Record the NCERT anchor for the answer

content_shape: stem carrying NOT / INCORRECT / FALSE / EXCEPT + 4 options
trap_mechanism: The reader solves the positive question and then picks a TRUE option. The negation inverts which option wins, so correct knowledge produces a wrong mark.
step_1: Circle the negation word before reading any option
step_2: Judge each option true or false on its own merits
step_3: Choose the one that FAILS, not the three that hold
step_4: Re-read the stem to confirm you answered the polarity asked

content_shape: stem with given quantities + 4 numeric options
trap_mechanism: Options are placed a factor or one decimal place apart, so a single arithmetic or unit slip lands exactly on a printed distractor instead of nowhere.
step_1: List the givens with their units
step_2: Write the governing relation before substituting anything
step_3: Carry units through to the result and check them
step_4: Ask which distractor a common slip would produce, and why yours is not it

trap_mechanism: The exponent, or its SIGN, is the only thing separating options. Scraped papers also flatten superscripts onto the baseline, which hides the difference entirely.
step_1: Rewrite every option in one common exponent form
step_2: Compute the mantissa separately from the exponent
step_3: Fix the sign of the exponent deliberately
step_4: Sanity-check the order of magnitude against physical reality

trap_mechanism: Options are algebraically near-identical, differing by a factor, a sign, or which variable carries the square.
how_to_spot: All four options render as math.
step_1: Derive the expression symbolically before looking at options
step_2: Check the dimensions of each option
step_4: Match the surviving form exactly, factor for factor

trap_mechanism: Knowing 2 of 4 pairings feels like progress but need not narrow the options to one.
how_to_spot: structure=match, options like 'A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I'.
step_1: Commit only the pairings you are certain of
step_2: Strike every option contradicting a certain pairing
step_3: Resolve what remains on the weakest pairing
step_4: Verify all four pairings of the chosen option

content_shape: as C06, with two options a single transposition apart
trap_mechanism: Two options differ by ONE swapped pairing, so the whole question turns on a single pair. (Agreeing on 3 of 4 is impossible -- fix three pairs of a bijection and the fourth is forced; a single swap agrees on exactly 2.)
how_to_spot: Two permutation options agree on exactly 2 of 4 pairings.
step_1: Find the one pairing the two surviving options disagree about
step_2: Decide that pairing on its own merits
step_3: Ignore the pairings the options already agree on
step_4: Confirm there is no second disagreement you missed

content_shape: stem + statements[2] + 4 options over the (I, II) truth pair
trap_mechanism: Mixed-truth pairs: one statement is true and the other is subtly false, usually on a qualifier rather than on the substance.
how_to_spot: structure=statement_i_ii, or two statements with no 'only' options.
step_1: Judge statement I alone as true or false
step_2: Judge statement II alone as true or false
step_3: Map the resulting (I, II) pair to the option that states it
step_4: Re-check qualifier words -- all, only, always, never

content_shape: stem + statements[3..5] + options like 'A and C only'
trap_mechanism: Partial knowledge maps cleanly onto a WRONG combination, and 'only' makes both the superset and the subset of the true set look defensible.
step_1: Judge every statement independently, writing each verdict down
step_2: Write out the true set explicitly before looking at options
step_3: Find the option matching that set exactly
step_4: Reject options that add one member or drop one

content_shape: stem + statements[A, R] + the fixed four-rung ladder
trap_mechanism: Both A and R are frequently true while R is NOT the explanation of A. That rung is the commonest miss on this shape, because verifying both statements feels like finishing.
step_3: If both are true, test separately whether R actually EXPLAINS A
step_4: Pick the rung matching that three-part verdict

trap_mechanism: Unanswerable without the figure. A missing, clipped or mis-cropped figure turns the item into a guess without ever looking unanswerable.
step_1: Confirm the figure is present and not clipped
step_2: Extract the quantities the figure carries, not the prose alone
step_4: Flag the item if any part of the figure is missing

trap_mechanism: Table structure collapses to a run-on digit string when scraped, destroying row and column alignment while leaving every digit present and plausible.
step_1: Rebuild rows and columns explicitly before solving
step_2: Restate the table as labelled pairs and check the count
step_3: Read the answer off the rebuilt table
step_4: Flag the item if alignment cannot be recovered with certainty

content_shape: stem asking increasing or decreasing order + 4 orderings
trap_mechanism: The correct sequence printed BACKWARDS is almost always one of the four options, so reading the direction wrong still lands on a printed answer.
how_to_spot: Stem says arrange / increasing / decreasing / order of.
step_1: Note which direction the stem demands
step_2: Rank the items on the stated property
step_3: Write the sequence in the demanded direction
step_4: Check that the reverse of your answer is not what you marked

trap_mechanism: Two options are identical as printed, so NO single correct answer exists in the source. Usually a lost radical, exponent or decimal point.
step_1: Magnify each duplicated option region separately
step_2: Look specifically for a lost radical, exponent, decimal or unit prefix
step_3: If still identical, mark the SOURCE defective
step_4: Never reconstruct the option -- flag it for better source material

content_shape: stem + 4 options that are pictures, absent from our source
trap_mechanism: The options are graphs, structures or circuits, and the scrape stored a placeholder instead of the image. The question looks complete but is unanswerable from our material.
how_to_spot: Option text matches 'Image option - will be added soon'.
step_1: Detect the placeholder before attempting a solve
step_2: Do not attempt to infer the pictures from the stem
step_4: Route it to re-acquisition from an official PDF
